title: Prompts become numbers: tokens and embeddings
hook: Follow a prompt to the tensor the sampler gets: byte-pair splitting, an embedding table that does not know its neighbours, and causal attention that does.

verified.claim: CLIPTextEncode tokenizes then encodes, and returns a list of tensor and dictionary pairs with pooled_output.
Start and end tokens are 49406 and 49407, with 77 positions.
Weights apply as (z - z_empty) * w + z_empty.
Long prompts are cut into chunks, not truncated.
embedding: is the identifier for embeddings, and backslash escapes keep a literal bracket.
BPE merges, table lookup and causal mask results are from running the lab.
The no-model text graph passes validate_prompt and ran on a CPU.

unchecked: The chunk table is worked out from reading the code. We did not encode real prompts with real weights.
The lab's attention uses random weights, so it shows structure and says nothing about meaning.
We read the warning for a missing embedding in the parser's code and did not trigger one.
